passage:
For one month, students kept a climate diary. They wrote down the weather, what they wore, how they traveled, and how much electricity their families used.
At first, the diary felt boring. Then students began noticing patterns. They used more air conditioning on days with less wind. They took scooters for trips short enough to walk. They bought cold drinks in plastic cups almost every afternoon.
The teacher did not ask them to feel guilty. She asked them to see connections.
By the end of the month, several students changed small habits. The diary showed that climate is a large issue, but daily choices are part of the large picture.
